title: Approve the Payment Run
scenario: It is 2:30 PM. The batch is assembled and the cutoff is 3:00 PM. Before money moves, one human puts their name on it: the AP Manager approves the run. Even in an automated desk, releasing funds is the moment that needs a person accountable. Learn what run approval confirms and why it stays human.
input: Payment Batch: 1 invoice, total 1220.00, 0 held, cutoff 3:00 PM. The AP Manager reviews the batch control totals and approves the run at 2:30 PM. Approval confirms the batch is complete and the totals are right; it is the single point where a human authorizes funds to leave Beacon.
instructions: Read run approval as the human control point before funds move.
Answer the four questions about who approves and what the approval confirms.
Validate to mint the run-approval record.

options.text: The AP Clerk who processed the invoices

questions.explain: Separation of duties: the Clerk processes invoices, the Manager approves the run. The person releasing funds is not the person who prepared them.

options.text: That the batch is complete and its control totals are correct
That each invoice is re-typed from scratch
That the vendor received the goods

questions.explain: The Manager checks the batch's count and total - the control figures - and confirms nothing was dropped or added. The line-level checks already happened upstream.

questions.prompt: Why keep a human here when everything upstream was automatic?

options.text: Because releasing funds is the highest-risk action and needs a named, accountable person
Because the software cannot add numbers
To slow the process down on purpose

questions.explain: Automation handles the judgment that can be encoded. Authorizing money to leave the company is deliberately kept human so there is always someone accountable for the release.

questions.prompt: The approval happens at 2:30 PM against a 3:00 PM cutoff. Why does timing matter?

options.text: It does not; approval can happen any time
Approval must land before the cutoff or the run misses today's payment window

questions.explain: The run has to be approved before the 3:00 PM cutoff to be delivered today. Approving at 2:30 leaves margin; miss the cutoff and payment slips to the next run.

artifactOnPass.confirms: batch complete and control totals correct

copilotPrompt: Explain run approval in a payables workflow: who approves it, what the approval confirms about the batch, why the release of funds stays human, and why the approval must beat the cutoff.
successMessage: Run approved. The AP Manager authorized the batch at 2:30 PM - funds are cleared to release before the 3:00 PM cutoff.

intro.heading: Before the run: one human on the release

sections.title: The moment money moves
sections.body: Everything before this was preparation. Run approval is the single point where funds are authorized to leave Beacon - the highest-risk action of the day, deliberately kept human.

sections.title: Separation of duties
sections.body: The AP Clerk prepared the invoices; the AP Manager approves the run. The person releasing money is never the person who prepared it - a foundational financial control.

sections.title: Confirm the controls, not the lines
sections.body: The Manager checks the batch count and total, confirming nothing was dropped or slipped in. The line-level matching already happened upstream and is not re-litigated here.

sections.title: Beat the cutoff
sections.body: Approval at 2:30 PM clears the 3:00 PM cutoff with margin. Miss the cutoff and the whole run waits for the next window - so timing is part of the control.

takeaway.heading: Run approved
points: You answered the four questions: who approves, what it confirms, why it stays human, and why timing matters.
Run approval is the one point where a named person authorizes funds to leave the company.
The AP Manager confirms the batch control totals, not the line-level checks already done upstream.
Approving at 2:30 PM clears the 3:00 PM cutoff, so the run ships today - captured in run-approval.json.
The workflow can now release a day of payments under a single accountable human approval.
